help.title: Go/No-Go Validation (Logistic Regression)
help.body:
Description
Go/No-Go Validation using Binary Logistic Regression (Probit/Normit link)

Purpose
Go/No-Go (attribute) gauges produce a binary pass/fail decision rather than a continuous measurement. This analysis uses binary logistic regression with a probit (normit) link function to model the probability of passing as a function of the true continuous input variable. It evaluates the measurement system's ability to correctly classify parts near the specification limit.
Following the AIAG MSA 4th Edition approach (Minitab MSA_VarIn.MAC by Thomas Rust), it estimates the transition point (where 50% of parts are classified as pass), quantifies measurement system variation, and computes key acceptance metrics.

Inputs
Variable Input (required) — the continuous measurement (e.g. diameter) for each part
Results (binary) (required) — the Go/No-Go gauge outcome (e.g. "Pass"/"Fail")
Pass Condition (required) — the exact string value in the Results column that means Pass
Individual / Summarized Results — whether each row is one measurement (Individual) or already summarized as counts of passes and total trials per input level (Summarized)
USL / LSL — specification limits; the limit being evaluated determines Bias and %GRR Tolerance
Evaluating Upper/Lower Limit — which spec limit the gauge is checking

Output Interpretation
Transition Point — the input value at which the gauge passes 50% of parts. Ideally equals the specification limit; any difference is the Bias.
MS Std Dev = |1/beta| where beta is the probit slope. Measures the spread of the gauge's decision boundary — smaller values indicate a sharper, more capable gauge.
95% Uncertainty = 2 × MS Std Dev — the zone around the transition point where classification is unreliable.
Bias = Transition Point − Specification. Non-zero bias means the gauge consistently accepts or rejects parts near the spec limit.
%Tol (Tolerance Ratio) = (6 × MS Std Dev) / Tolerance × 100. Primary acceptance criterion: below 10% acceptable, 10–30% marginal, above 30% unacceptable.
%Bias of Tolerance = |Bias| / Tolerance × 100.

Go/No-Go Validation plot — shows observed pass proportions (dots) and the fitted probit S-curve. A coloured band below shows: red = confident Fail zone, grey hatched = uncertainty zone (Transition ± U), green = confident Pass zone.

Binary Fitted Line Plot (optional) — shows the fitted probit curve with 95% confidence bands, useful for assessing model fit.

Deviance Residual Plots (optional) — four diagnostic panels for the logistic regression model (Normal Probability, vs Normit of Fits, Histogram, vs Order).
